title: one KV head to many logical KV heads
hypothesis: One physical K/V projection and one stored K/V cache per token, expanded through per-query-head Mirror coordinates at read time, can recover a shared-view four-head attention teacher with lower actual cache bytes than MQA/GQA/full MHA; arbitrary K/V roles should require more physical/private state.
physical_object: one shared K/V projection pair and one persistent K/V cache stream
mirror_coordinate: per-query-head Givens coordinates on projected K and V head channels
logical_multiplicity: four query heads with four distinct logical K/V views from one cached physical K/V head

teacher_modes.shared_kv_views: one physical K/V pair plus four fixed head views

task.storage_metric: actual persistent KV cache bytes per sequence, plus serialized model payload bytes

controls: full MHA with four K/V projection pairs
MQA with one repeated K/V pair
MQA plus per-head rank-1 K/V residuals
MQA cache plus per-head Mirror K/V views

development.selection_metric: mean held-out attention-output MSE pooled across methods and teacher modes

storage.authority: actual serialized inference payload bytes and exact tensor cache bytes
storage.cache_formula: 2 * physical KV heads * head_dim * cached sequence length * bytes per element

success_gate: In all three fresh shared-KV-view worlds, Mirror output MSE <=1.10x full MHA, actual model payload and persistent cache bytes are both below full MHA, and it beats MQA/GQA on output MSE at lower combined model+cache bytes. Report cache read/compute and runtime separately.
failure_gate: Mirror misses output-quality gate in two or more fresh aligned worlds, or ordinary MQA/GQA achieves same quality with equal/lower combined storage and compute. Independent K/V failure alone is a structural boundary.
boundaries: teacher is deliberately generated from shared K/V plus views
fixed-update screen, not capacity near convergence
cache bandwidth is a proxy, not measured GPU memory traffic
